chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed to one of his heirs that he had a debt due from him (the deceased). He said: If the deceased was in a state of illness, then give to the one to whom he bequeathed.

key_terms.مَرْضِيًّا: in a state of illness (specifically deathbed illness)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a bequest to an heir for a debt if the deceased was ill?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the distinction between a debt repayment and a bequest (hibah) when a dying person acknowledges a debt to one of their heirs; Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that if the deceased was ill at the time, the amount is treated as a gift in addition to the heir's fixed inheritance share, preventing the deduction of the same amount from the estate. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it protects the heir from losing their statutory portion while still fulfilling the deceased's obligation, reflecting the principle that a bequest to an heir is valid but distinct from debt settlement unless specified otherwise. The context of 'marad al-mawt' (death illness) is crucial here, as it determines the timing of the legal status of the bequest relative to the final distribution of the estate.
